purpose: ASVS V3.3.5 had no decision. It asks that a cookie's name and value together stay under 4096 bytes, because a browser handed a larger one stores nothing and reports nothing: the write succeeds on the server, the value never comes back, and every control that depends on the cookie fails with no message anywhere. One cookie in this repository was genuinely over that limit. pc_staff_access_meta carried encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(metadata)) where metadata.reason is operator free text the API accepts up to 2000 characters; percent-encoding costs six bytes per Cyrillic character, so a 526-character Russian reason produced a 4097-byte cookie and a 2000-character one produced 12946 bytes. The staff access session was activated upstream and then failed every later authorization read, silently.
requiredInvariants: The defect is measured, not asserted. 526 is the shortest all-Cyrillic reason that takes pc_staff_access_meta past 4096 bytes with this record shape; an all-ASCII reason at the DTO maximum of 2000 reaches only 2946 bytes and never trips it. Both numbers are computed in the test file, not quoted from memory.

Only the reason is shortened, and only in the cookie. That is safe because nothing reads it back from there: verifiedSessionContext compares accessSessionId, staffRole, accessMode and expiresAt; the revoke path compares accessSessionId; and the activation response returns the untruncated reason straight from the database. Those are all four readers of the cookie in the repository, enumerated rather than assumed.

A record that already fits serializes byte-for-byte as it did before. Spreading over an existing key keeps its position, so JSON key order is unchanged, and a test asserts the identity against the previous expression.

The cut is on a code point, never through a surrogate pair. The first version of that test passed against a deliberately broken implementation because the budget happened to run out on a character boundary; the test now sweeps eight prefix offsets so at least one lands mid-pair.

When the remaining fields cannot fit on their own, the activation is undone upstream and reported as STAFF_SESSION_METADATA_TOO_LARGE. Writing a cookie the browser will discard would leave an activated session no later request can present. This path is unreachable with today's field shapes - permissions is a bounded enum and the ids are UUIDs - and is tested at the function, not claimed at the route.

Every one of the 78 cookie writes under apps/web and apps/api/src is now either a literal or measured at the write. 35 are literals, 43 pass through bounded-cookie.ts. apps/api/src contains none, which the same scan establishes rather than assumes.

The guard enumerates by git mode and skips symlinks. apps/web carries a tracked mirror of relative symlinks, and the first run of this guard reported on apps/web/apps/web/middleware.ts while never opening apps/web/middleware.ts at all.

boundedCookieValue throws rather than dropping the write. A caller that can legitimately exceed the budget must decide what to shorten; a caller that cannot has a bug, and a failed request reports it better than a session that looks issued and does not work.
TextEncoder, not Buffer: apps/web/middleware.ts runs on the Edge runtime.

V10.2.1's evidence was re-bound, not loosened. Wrapping the gov-id state write broke a pattern that matched the old syntax; the pattern now names the new one and still falsifies - pointing the state cookie at the nonce rejects the decision again.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation. No registration business logic, 1C, marketing or presentation change.

Three existing tests assert cookie-write syntax by scanning source, and wrapping the values broke them. Each was re-bound to the new shape, never relaxed: the two minting regexes now also require the budget wrapper, which narrows the match; the locale and CSRF assertions name the wrapped call. Each was re-falsified afterwards - a second file minting the access cookie from an upstream payload, and pointing the locale cookie at a constant, both fail again.

The budget wrapper was checked for being a hiding place rather than assumed not to be. The session-marker assertion previously matched only the bare form; a literal 1 written as boundedCookieValue(SESSION_COOKIE, '1') now fails it too.
acceptance: node scripts/security/verify-cookie-size-bound.mjs exits 0: 78 inspected, 35 literal, 43 bounded, 0 unaccounted for.
ASVS V3.3.5 moves NOT_ASSESSED to PASS: PASS 129 to 130, NOT_ASSESSED 39 to 38, FAIL and NOT_APPLICABLE unchanged, rejected decisions back to the single pre-existing V8.2.4.
Revocable in three directions: disabling the budget check rejects V3.3.5; replacing the fitted serialization rejects V3.3.5; pointing the gov-id state cookie at the nonce rejects V10.2.1.
Eight negative mutations each fail a named test.

Full apps/web vitest run, twice on this commit. Before the three source-scanning assertions were re-bound: 227 failed files / 376 failed tests / 5212 passed, against a main baseline of 224 / 373 / 5199 - exactly the three this refactor invalidated. After re-binding: 224 failed files / 373 failed tests / 5215 passed, the baseline plus the 16 new tests, with no failing file moved in either direction.
